target_intervention_label: Comprehensive genomic profiling (paired DNA + RNA NGS, plus HER2 IHC/ISH and MMR IHC)
comment: No argument here: every axis is ngs_pending, so the paired DNA+RNA panel with an RNA fusion arm is the one move that unlocks all the rest, and it costs the patient nothing. Insist the RNA arm is in the order, since a DNA-only panel can miss the FGFR2 fusions that carry the biggest upside on this board.

target_intervention_label: Ivosidenib (only if an IDH1 R132 mutation is confirmed)
comment: Ranking ivosidenib at 3 on the strength of its clean safety ledger while banishing lirafugratinib entirely undersells the trade a balanced 0.5 weight actually allows: ivosidenib's ORR is 2% (pmid:32416072) against the ReFocus cohort's 46.5% (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476). If FGFR2 confirms, the selective agent's 32.8% grade 3+ PPE is a real but manageable cost for a tenfold-better response, not a reason to keep it off the ranked list.

target_intervention_label: Comprehensive genomic profiling (paired DNA + RNA NGS with fusion calling, MSI, TMB) + HER2 IHC/ISH and MMR IHC
comment: Agreed, and the provenance catch is a good one: NCT07359820 excludes CCA, so the ReFocus cohort is the on-axis data to cite. The gate ranks first for the same reason I rank it first: nothing downstream is real until the panel reads out.

Elevating ivosidenib to rank 2 purely because it is the lone RCT, then dropping lirafugratinib to rank 4 as abstract-only, weights design tier over what the patient gets: ClarIDHy's own ORR is 2% and the ITT OS missed alpha (HR 0.69, p=0.060, pmid:32416072). The FGFR2-selective 46.5% ORR (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476) is single-arm and pre-approval, which I concede, but a randomized read on a 2% response is a clean answer to the wrong question if the FGFR2 axis lights up.

target_intervention_label: Ivosidenib (if IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor NGS)
comment: The NCCN category-1 badge is doing all the lifting for rank 1, but it sits on a PFS win of 2.7 vs 1.4 months and a 2% ORR (pmid:32416072), which is the thinnest actionable signal on the board. If futibatinib's FGFR2 axis reads positive, its 42% ORR and 21.7-month OS (pmid:36652354) is the pick I would put in front of the patient first, and guideline lettering should not bury a tenfold response difference under an IDH1 call that is no more likely to be positive.

target_intervention_label: Lirafugratinib (RLY-4008), FGFR2-selective, via the ReFocus cohort
comment: This is the one other position that puts the FGFR2-selective magnitude bet where it belongs, rank 2 behind the gate, on ORR 46.5% and mPFS 11.3 mo (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476). We are aligned; my only caution is that the abstract-only status and Sept 2026 PDUFA mean access runs through the ReFocus slot or expanded access, so line that up alongside the panel rather than assuming an on-label prescription.

Seating lirafugratinib at rank 1 puts an ASCO GI 2026 abstract with no PubMed record and no registration-scale safety follow-up above pemigatinib, which has carried an FDA label since 2020. You name the abstract weakness yourself, so I will name the safety one you skip past: grade 3+ palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia ran 32.8% (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476), and hand-foot at that grade is a dose-limiting, quality-of-life event, not a footnote. The FGFR2-selective design does spare FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia, which I credit, but sparing one on-target toxicity while carrying a 32.8% grade 3 skin toxicity with no mature long-tail data is not a cleaner safety bet than the approved agent. The specific missing datum is durable tolerability at approval scale; until the PDUFA read and a peer-reviewed safety table land, I do not rank it above pemigatinib.

The 52.9% response rate you cite for gunagratinib comes off n=17 in an abstract (doi:10.1200/JCO.2023.41.4_suppl.572), and a safety ledger built on seventeen patients cannot characterize the long-tail toxicity my prior turns on. The reported grade 3+ TEAE rate of 35.3%, led by transaminase elevation and nail disorders, is a first look, not a stable estimate, and the confidence band on both the efficacy and the safety numbers is wide at that n. I do not object to holding gunagratinib as a trial-enrollment option on a confirmed FGFR2 fusion, and I credit that it recorded no treatment-related deaths and no AE-driven discontinuations in that small series. But ranking it into the therapeutic five ahead of agents with registration-scale safety populations reaches past what seventeen patients can support.

You rank lirafugratinib second and call it the best-tolerated option on the FGFR axis for a balanced weight. That claim rests on the hyperphosphatemia comparison alone and skips the toxicity that actually differentiates it: grade 3+ palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia at 32.8% plus grade 3+ stomatitis at 12.1% (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476). Trading away FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia for a one-in-three grade 3 hand-foot rate is a lateral move on tolerability, not an improvement, and grade 3 hand-foot is the kind of dose-interrupting, function-limiting event a patient feels every day. Pemigatinib's on-target hyperphosphatemia was 55% any grade with no grade 3-4 (pmid:32203698), which is a milder grade distribution at the same axis. Under a 0.5 weight I would not call the abstract-stage selective agent the tolerability winner over the approved one; the grade-3 arithmetic points the other way.

You seat futibatinib above pemigatinib on a kinase-domain resistance sequencing edge, which is a real point in the second-line setting but is not where a treatment-naive patient starts. In the first-line FGFR2 slot the toxicity gap runs the other way: grade 3 hyperphosphatemia hit 30% on futibatinib (pmid:36652354) against no grade 3-4 events on pemigatinib, where the on-target effect was 55% any grade (pmid:32203698). At a comparable response rate I take the lower-grade burden and the longer post-approval record, so within the lane I reverse your order. The resistance-mutation coverage is a genuine reason to switch to futibatinib after pemigatinib progression, and I would document that as the sequencing plan rather than as the reason to lead with the higher grade-3 agent.

We land in the same place on the HER2 axis and I want the record to show it: you kept T-DXd off your ranked five and seated zanidatamab at rank 5 instead, which is exactly the ordering I argue for on safety. Adjudicated drug-related ILD ran 10.5% with three treatment-related deaths (pmid:37870536), and intake supplied no pulmonary baseline, no organ-function labs, and no DLCO to gate against, so the mitigation an ILD signal demands is not on file. Because no persona ranked T-DXd above zanidatamab, this stays a shared downgrade rather than a formal veto. Zanidatamab covers the same axis at a 3% grade-3 ejection-fraction signal with a standard echo algorithm (pmid:37423227). If T-DXd re-enters at all, it should be gated on a confirmed HER2 IHC 3+ read plus a baseline pulmonary assessment and a written ILD-monitoring plan; on a true 3+ tumor with that plan in place I would not block it.

Placing zanidatamab above T-DXd on the patient's behalf is the right safety call and I back it fully, even though no toxicity veto was set in preferences. The reasoning holds on its own terms: an adjudicated 10.5% ILD rate with three treatment-related deaths on T-DXd (pmid:37870536) against a 3% grade-3 ejection-fraction signal on zanidatamab that inherits the cardiac-monitoring algorithm built over decades of trastuzumab use (pmid:37423227). One thing to tighten in the framing: the gate is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH, not the NGS amplification call, so the rank-1 workup has to carry the protein readout or this pick cannot be selected correctly. And with no baseline cardiac function supplied at intake, the echo monitoring you cite is a plan to schedule, not one already confirmed feasible.

We land in the same place and I want to sharpen one word. You sell ivosidenib on 'randomized evidence,' and ClarIDHy is the only RCT here (RoB2:Low), so that is fair. But the randomized endpoint that actually cleared alpha is PFS (HR 0.37, p<0.0001). The survival read did not: ITT OS was HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.44-1.1, p=0.060 (pmid:32416072). The 0.46 you cite is an RPSFT crossover adjustment after 70% of placebo patients crossed, which is a sensitivity model, not the trial's OS result. For a do-no-harm pick that is fine, the tolerability case carries it, but the phrase 'randomized evidence' should attach to delayed progression, not to a survival benefit the trial never demonstrated at conventional alpha.

You already named the ITT OS caveat in your own concern list, so credit where it is due, most personas glossed it. My qualifier is on what the category-1 label actually rests on. NCCN v2.2025 graded ivosidenib category 1 off the PFS primary (HR 0.37) with crossover-adjusted OS support, not off a survival endpoint that separated. So when you seat it at rank 1 on 'the strongest guideline anchor,' the anchor is a PFS win plus modeling, which is thinner than a category-1 badge reads to a casual eye. That is a fair rank-1 given the RCT pedigree, but the anchor is the PFS endpoint, and I would not let the category number stand in for a survival claim that ITT OS (p=0.060, pmid:32416072) does not support.

You rank abstract-only data at 2 and call it 'enrollable now,' and I think that overstates what we can stand on. ReFocus reads ORR 46.5% (95% CI 37.1-56.1) in n=114, single-arm, but it is an ASCO GI 2026 abstract with no PubMed record and a ROBINS-I:Moderate placeholder on a paper none of us has read (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476). Against two FGFR2 agents with peer-reviewed pivotals (futibatinib ORR 42%, pmid:36652354; pemigatinib 35.5%, pmid:32203698), a moderate confidence at rank 2 is more than the evidence maturity supports. Credit on provenance: you cited NCT04526106, the ReFocus cohort, correctly, not the non-CCA basket NCT07359820 that some conflate. I would drop this to a trial-enrollment option behind the approved agents until the full paper lets us audit response ascertainment and censoring.

Seating an abstract at rank 1 is exactly the trade I push back on. The 46.5% ORR (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476) is a single-arm number with no comparator, no PMID, and no full text to check how responses were adjudicated, and the drug is pre-approval (PDUFA pending). You concede all of that and rank it first anyway on magnitude. My objection is not the tolerability argument for FGFR2-selective design, which is real, it is putting an unaudited abstract above futibatinib's NEJM pivotal (ORR 42%, mOS 21.7 mo, pmid:36652354). One thing you got right that others muddle: the enrollment route is the ReFocus cohort (NCT04526106), not the basket NCT07359820, which excludes CCA outright. Rank the peer-reviewed agent first; keep the selective drug as the upside bet it currently is.

You give a ranked slot to a 52.9% ORR that is 9 of 17 patients (doi:10.1200/JCO.2023.41.4_suppl.572), abstract-only, ROBINS-I:Serious, with no confidence interval reported. You say the CI is wide enough to drive a truck through, and then rank it fourth anyway. On n=17 the Wilson interval around 52.9% runs roughly 31 to 74%, so that point estimate is compatible with activity well below the approved FGFR2 agents. This is a hypothesis, not a rankable option: no comparator, tiny sample, unread full text. I would move it off the ranked list into the trial-consideration lane with tinengotinib's 11-patient subset (ORR 27.3%, ROBINS-I:Serious, pmid:38297981), which is the honest company for a number this underpowered.

Ranking lirafugratinib first over approved futibatinib and pemigatinib inverts the guideline order: it is under FDA priority review with a 27 Sep 2026 PDUFA, so it is not approved and not listed in NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025, while futibatinib and pemigatinib are both category 2A there. On a confirmed FGFR2 fusion the guideline-consonant use of the ReFocus data (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476) is trial enrollment, not a standard rec displacing the two approved agents. Burying ivosidenib at rank 6 also passes over the only NCCN category-1 anchor in this whole set.

The 2% ORR and 2.7-vs-1.4-month PFS (pmid:32416072) are exactly why ivosidenib sits at rank 6 here, but NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 read that same ClarIDHy result, crossover-blunted OS and all, and still graded it category 1 for IDH1-mutant subsequent-line disease. That grade reflects a randomized win no other axis in this dossier can match. Effect size is your lens and I take the point, but category 1 is not a badge to file at the bottom of the list.

target_intervention_label: Pemigatinib (only if an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement is confirmed)
comment: No quarrel with the CGP gate or with favoring the longer-approved FGFR agent on safety-follow-up depth, and both pemigatinib and futibatinib are NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 category 2A. The one thing I would flag: ivosidenib is now category 1 in that same version for IDH1-mutant disease, the sole category-1 listing in the set, so among the biomarker-conditional therapies it has a firmer consensus footing than the rank-3 slot behind pemigatinib and ivosidenib implies. Not a safety objection, just a guideline-weight one.

We land on the same rank-2 placement and I agree the ITT OS missed alpha (HR 0.69, p=0.060, pmid:32416072), so the precision is fair. Worth adding to the record: the NCCN panel had that non-significant ITT OS and the RPSFT-adjusted 0.46 in front of it and still made ivosidenib category 1 in Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 on the PFS win, so the category-1 grade is the panel's calibration of the same evidence you are reading, not a number that skipped the caveat. That is a reason to name it category 1 explicitly rather than treat the listing as softer than the data.

target_intervention_label: Lirafugratinib (RLY-4008), FGFR2-selective, via the ReFocus cohort (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed)
comment: The prefers_trials preference makes lirafugratinib a legitimate enrollment option once FGFR2 confirms, and to your credit you named futibatinib as the on-label fallback. But ranking the pre-approval agent at 2, above approved futibatinib, still reads as a standard rec over a NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 category-2A agent, and lirafugratinib is neither approved (PDUFA 27 Sep 2026) nor NCCN-listed. The guideline-consonant framing is a trial slot sitting alongside the approved FGFR pair, not ahead of it in the treatment order.

target_intervention_label: Zanidatamab (FDA-approved, on-label; if HER2 IHC-positive with reflex ISH confirmed)
comment: This one is squarely guideline-consonant: zanidatamab is NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 category 2A for HER2-positive subsequent-line disease off the dedicated HERIZON-BTC-01 cohort (pmid:37423227), and putting it ahead of basket-route T-DXd matches how the guideline treats the biliary-specific trial. The IHC-plus-reflex-ISH gate you name is the right one, not an NGS amplification call. Agreement here, not qualification.

You put lirafugratinib in a 'trial-enrollment lane, not the ranked set' because it is not yet approved or NCCN-listed, and for a guideline-anchored read that is consistent. But the patient set prefers_trials=true, and the ReFocus cohort (NCT04526106, doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476) is a recruiting on-axis route with ORR 46.5% and the lowest hyperphosphatemia burden on the FGFR lane. Under the one preference on file, an enrollable next-gen agent is exactly what should be surfaced first, not fenced off from the ranked menu.

Keeping comprehensive genomic profiling as the rank-1 gating workup even while ivosidenib takes the top therapeutic slot is the right call for this patient, since every axis is ngs_pending and nothing else can be acted on until the panel reads. The IDH1 pick itself sits fine against a balanced 0.5 weight: oral, near-placebo grade 3+, and an open registration trial (NCT02989857) that serves prefers_trials. My only ask is that the CGP gate stay explicitly ahead of it in what the patient sees, not just in your notes.

Your evidence discount is fair and the provenance flag is worth keeping: the ReFocus readout is abstract-only, and NCT07359820 does exclude CCA so nobody should cite it as the route (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476, nct:NCT04526106). Where I pull back is calling it 'investigational, not an on-label option' as the reason it sits below the approved agents. For a patient who set prefers_trials=true, pre-approval status is not a demotion; the recruiting ReFocus cohort is a live door, and the preference asks me to put it in front of them alongside the on-label picks, not beneath them by default.

target_intervention_label: Comprehensive genomic profiling (paired DNA + RNA NGS)
comment: Rank-1 for the paired DNA+RNA panel is the pick that most directly serves this patient: it unlocks all eight axes, carries no toxicity to weigh against the 0.5 preference, and it is the precondition for every trial the prefers_trials flag asks us to surface. Your insistence on the RNA arm and on IHC/ISH for HER2 rather than an NGS copy-number stand-in is what keeps the highest-yield doors from reading falsely shut. No tension with any preference field here, so I endorse without qualification.

Holding T-DXd below zanidatamab on the 10.5% adjudicated ILD rate and three treatment-related deaths in DESTINY-PanTumor02 is the call I would make on the patient's behalf too (pmid:37870536 vs pmid:37423227). No toxicity veto was set, so I cannot dress this as a hard filter, but a balanced 0.5 weight does not point toward the ILD-risk ADC when a comparably active antibody covers the same HER2 axis at a manageable 3% grade-3 ejection-fraction signal. If T-DXd is offered at all, it should come with a baseline pulmonary read and a written ILD-monitoring plan attached.

Defaulting to pemigatinib on depth of post-approval safety follow-up is defensible, and the concern about immature registration-scale tolerability for the selective agents is real, I grant that. But you set aside lirafugratinib partly on 'no US access,' and the ReFocus cohort is actively recruiting (NCT04526106), which for a prefers_trials=true patient is an open door rather than a closed one (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476). At a balanced 0.5 weight, its FGFR2-selective profile sparing FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia is a live tolerability argument the patient's preference asks us to at least surface next to pemigatinib, not omit.

Seating the FGFR2-selective agent at the head of the therapeutic picks and lining up trial or expanded-access enrollment in parallel with the panel is exactly what prefers_trials=true asks for, so from the patient's lens I am with you (doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.476, nct:NCT04526106). Leaving T-DXd off over the ILD signal with no organ-function labs supplied also reads as user-protective under a balanced 0.5 weight, not just a risk call. My one caution is that you name the abstract-only maturity plainly to the patient, which you did, so this holds.
